gel_data_resources  (read-only)
===================

Outputs of the Genomics England bioinformatics pipelines and other resources,
mounted on the desktop (~/gel_data_resources) and the HPC (/gel_data_resources).

  main_programme/        100,000 Genomes Project datasets (by type, then date)
  gms/                   NHS Genomic Medicine Service datasets
  pilot/                 pilot programme datasets
  example_config_files/  configuration templates for R, Python and the LabKey API
  example_scripts/       example scripts (LabKey API queries, workshops)
  workflows/             pipelines provided for researchers

This folder is read-only. Writing here gives "Permission denied": to unpack a
file, write the output elsewhere, e.g.  gunzip -c file.gz > ~/re_gecip/.../file

[Training simulator: the large datasets are not included. Practicals add the
files they need.]

Configuration templates.

Desktop:   cd $HOME && cp -rf ~/gel_data_resources/example_config_files/Workspaces/. .
HPC:       cp -rf /gel_data_resources/example_config_files/Double_Helix/. ./

Then edit ~/.netrc: put your username (initial + last name, e.g. jdoe) and your
RE password in place of yourusername / yourPasswordHere, and make the file
private:   chmod 600 ~/.netrc
The LabKey API reads your credentials from ~/.netrc.

http_proxy=http://pfsense.int.corp.gel.ac:3128
ftp_proxy=http://pfsense.int.corp.gel.ac:3128
rsync_proxy=http://pfsense.int.corp.gel.ac:3128
https_proxy=http://pfsense.int.corp.gel.ac:3128
no_proxy=localhost,127.0.0.1,localaddress,.localdomain.com,.gel.zone,.cluster

# R configuration for the Research Environment.
# In the real RE these lines point R at Genomics England's internal CRAN and
# Bioconductor mirrors (an Artifactory server). The training simulator keeps
# R's own repository settings so that install.packages() still works here.

# myrepo["CRAN"] = "https://artifactory.aws.gel.ac/artifactory/cran"      # (real RE)
options(repos = myrepo)
rm(myrepo)

Example scripts.

  labkey_api/query_to_df.R      the R helper for LabKey SQL queries, with an example
  labkey_api/query_to_df.py     the same in Python
  labkey_api/select_rows.R      fetching (part of) a whole table with labkey.selectRows
  workshop_scripts/             materials of training sessions

Copy a script into your own folder before changing it:
  cp ~/gel_data_resources/example_scripts/labkey_api/query_to_df.R ~/re_gecip/training/$USER/

# Query the LabKey tables with SQL from R.
# Before the first use: configure ~/.netrc (see ~/gel_data_resources/example_config_files).

library(tidyverse)
library(Rlabkey)

labkey.setWafEncoding(FALSE)

query_to_df <- function(sql_query, database) {
  labkey.setDefaults(baseUrl = "https://labkey.prod.aws.gel.ac/labkey/")
  labkey.executeSql(folderPath = database,
                    schemaName = "lists",
                    colNameOpt = "rname",
                    sql = sql_query) %>%
    mutate(across(everything(), as.character))
}

# Query the LabKey tables with SQL from Python.
# Before the first use: configure ~/.netrc (see ~/gel_data_resources/example_config_files).
import labkey
import pandas as pd
from labkey.api_wrapper import APIWrapper


def query_to_df(sql_query, database):
    api = APIWrapper(domain="labkey.prod.aws.gel.ac", container_path=database,
                     context_path="labkey", use_ssl=True)
    results = api.query.execute_sql(sql=sql_query, schema_name="lists",
                                    max_rows=100000000, waf_encode_sql=False)
    return pd.DataFrame(results["rows"])


database = "/main-programme/main-programme_v19_2024-10-31"
sql = """
SELECT participant_id, programme, year_of_birth, participant_phenotypic_sex
FROM participant
WHERE programme_consent_status = 'Consenting'
"""
df = query_to_df(sql, database)
print(df.head())
print(df["programme"].value_counts())

# Fetch a whole table, or part of one, with labkey.selectRows.
library(Rlabkey)
labkey.setDefaults(baseUrl = "https://labkey.prod.aws.gel.ac/labkey/")

participant <- labkey.selectRows(
  schemaName = "lists",
  colNameOpt = "rname",
  maxRows = 100000000,
  folderPath = "/main-programme/main-programme_v19_2024-10-31",
  queryName = "participant",
  colFilter = makeFilter(c("participant_type", "EQUAL", "Proband"),
                         c("year_of_birth", "BETWEEN", "1950,2010")),
  colSelect = c("participant_id", "rare_diseases_family_id", "year_of_birth"),
  colSort = "+year_of_birth"
)
nrow(participant)

bcftools plugins – a small synthetic example
============================================

Training simulator: these files are synthetic. They describe no real person: a
made-up family (child, father, mother) and an unrelated sample, on a made-up
1,000-base chromosome "chr1". They come from the genomics-wasm project
(https://github.com/comparativechrono/genomics-wasm, datasets/hts/common/, MIT
licence), which uses them to check its builds of bcftools.

  trio-csq.vcf   12 variants of four samples, with VEP-style annotations in the
                 CSQ field (Allele|Consequence|IMPACT|SYMBOL|Gene|Feature|...),
                 missing, haploid and multiallelic genotypes, and Mendelian errors
  phased.vcf     the same samples, with phased genotypes
  family.ped     the pedigree of the trio

Try (module load bcftools/1.21 first; the folder is read-only, so write any
output into your own folder):

  D=/gel_data_resources/example_scripts/workshop_scripts/bcftools_plugins
  bcftools +split-vep $D/trio-csq.vcf -l
  bcftools +split-vep $D/trio-csq.vcf -d -f '%CHROM\t%POS\t%Consequence\t%SYMBOL\n'
  bcftools +fill-tags $D/trio-csq.vcf -Ov -o ~/filled.vcf -- -t AN,AC,AF
  bcftools +mendelian2 $D/trio-csq.vcf -P $D/family.ped -m c
  bcftools +trio-switch-rate $D/phased.vcf -- -p $D/family.ped

With bcftools/1.16 the Mendelian plugin is the older one:
  bcftools +mendelian $D/trio-csq.vcf -p $D/family.ped -m c

Notices for the files in this folder
====================================

tumor.bam, normal.bam (and their .bai indexes) hold reads of the cell lines HCC1395 (a breast cancer) and HCC1395BL
(B lymphocytes of the same donor), sequenced by the SEQC2 consortium (Sequencing Quality Control Phase 2, led by the
US FDA) and released by NCBI for benchmarking: study SRP162370,
https://ftp-trace.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/ReferenceSamples/seqc/Somatic_Mutation_WG/data/WGS/ .
reference.fa is two windows of chromosome 21 of the human reference GRCh38, from UCSC (hg38). truth.vcf holds records
of the SEQC2 high-confidence somatic SNV and indel truth set v1.2.1.

These are publicly distributed research data. Please cite:

  Fang LT, Zhu B, Zhao Y, et al. Establishing community reference samples, data and call sets for benchmarking
  cancer mutation detection using whole-genome sequencing. Nature Biotechnology 2021; 39: 1151-1160.
  doi:10.1038/s41587-021-00993-6

The files were prepared – the reads of two windows, moved onto the windows, nothing else changed – by the genomics-wasm
project (https://github.com/comparativechrono/genomics-wasm, commit bfacba3: datasets/strelka2/hcc1395), whose
manifest records every source, byte range and step. Where every file came from, and its SHA-256: provenance.json
(in the workbench's data/examples/somatic).
